zh: (1157-99) the king of England from 1189 to 1199, following his father King Henry II. He is often called Richard the Lionheart or Richard, Coeur de Lion, because of his courage in battle. He spent the first part of his rule abroad fighting in the Third Crusade, at the end of which he reached a peace agreement with Saladin in 1191. On his journey home he was captured and held as a prisoner by the Austrian emperor (= ruler) Henry VI, until a large amount of money was paid for releasing him. He spent his later years fighting against the French, and after his death in battle in 1199 he was replaced as king by his brother John.

zh: (1367-1400) the king of England from 1377 to 1399, following his grandfather King Edward III. He became king at the age of 10, relying on his uncle John of Gaunt to help rule the country, and was successful in defeating the Peasants' Revolt of 1381. The rest of his rule was spent trying to control the other powerful men of the country, particularly Henry Bolingbroke, John of Gaunt's son. In 1398 Richard sent Henry abroad, but he returned the following year and took power, ruling as King Henry IV. Richard was put in prison, where he died, possibly murdered.

en: a first name for boys, short for Richard
to hit a surface and come off it fast at a different angle
ex: The bullet ricocheted off a nearby wall.
子弹从附近的一面墙上弹飞了。

zh: a type of soft white Italian cheese
en: a type of soft white Italian cheese
ex: spinach and ricotta cannelloni
菠菜和意大利乳清干酪碎肉卷子

zh: 扭曲（或怪笑）的嘴；龇牙咧嘴
en: a wide twisted or smiling mouth that does not look natural or relaxed
to remove something that is causing a problem from a place, group, etc.
ex: Further measures will be taken to rid our streets of crime.
将采取进一步的措施来防止街头犯罪。

en: to make yourself free from somebody/something that is annoying you or causing you a problem
ex: to rid yourself of guilt
摆脱内疚

zh: 充满（某种不良事物）的；满是…的
en: full of a particular unpleasant thing
ex: a disease-ridden slum
疾病流行的贫民窟

zh: 神秘事件；无法解释的情况
en: a question that is difficult to understand, and that has a surprising answer, that you ask somebody as a game
ex: Stop talking in riddles (= saying things that are confusing)—say what you mean.
别拐弯抹角了，有话直说。

en: to sit on an animal, especially a horse, and control it as it moves
ex: I learnt to ride as a child.
我小时候就学会了骑马。

w: Ride a Cock-horse to Banbury Cross
uk: /ˌraɪd ə kɒk ˌhɔːs tə ˌbænbəri ˈkrɒs/
us: /ˌraɪd ə kɑːk ˌhɔːrs tə ˌbænbəri ˈkrɔːs/
zh: a traditional nursery rhyme, often said by mothers to their babies as they bounce them on their knee. A 'cock-horse' is a child's toy, a horse's head on a stick. The words are: “Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross,To see a fine lady upon a white horse;Rings on her fingers and bells on her toes,And she shall have music wherever she goes.”
en: a traditional nursery rhyme, often said by mothers to their babies as they bounce them on their knee. A 'cock-horse' is a child's toy, a horse's head on a stick. The words are: “Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross,To see a fine lady upon a white horse;Rings on her fingers and bells on her toes,And she shall have music wherever she goes.”
to depend on something
ex: My whole future is riding on this interview.
我的未来全靠这次面试了。

zh: 安然渡过（难关）；经受得住
en: to manage to survive a difficult situation or time without having to make great changes
ex: Do you think we can ride out the recession?
您认为我们可以度过衰退吗？

zh: 慢慢向上移动；渐渐缩上去
en: to move gradually upwards, out of position
ex: Short skirts tend to ride up when you sit down.
坐下来的时候，短裙就会往上收。

en: an extra part of a competition in which horses that have the same score jump again to decide the winner

zh: 骑手；骑马（或自行车、摩托车）的人
en: a person who rides a horse, bicycle or motorcycle
ex: Three riders (= people riding horses) were approaching.
三个骑马的人越来越近。
